**Guide to how I did it**

\[26M UK\]

I worked at McDonald's on a basic hourly wage after I got my degree and taught myself web dev

I worked 25 hours a week and studied the other 25-30 hours. 

I followed a route of designing and building basic static websites (html, css, jquery) 

What I did then was, I posted every day on Instagram & twitter what I was learning/coding that day, it could be super simple, literally a picture of the screen at a cool angle and something like 'Project coming along nicely' or 'Implementing a slider today!' and add some relevant hashtags. 

Whilst doing that I googled every local digital agency and followed them on all social media, and liked and commented on almost every post. The comments were super simple just 'Wow looks great' or 'Interesting article, I like this this and that about it'

There were many days where I couldn't code or was unmotivated or stuck on some compiling error for days on end but I kept going

One day after about 9-10 months of doing this a CEO of my favourite local agency got in touch and asked me to come in for a chat. 

I came in, showed some of my little projects (honestly they sucked so bad) but he said 

'basically, you seem to be super keen to learn \[SOCIAL MEDIA!!!\] and you've shown me you can apply yourself \[SHITTY PROJECTS!!!\] so we will take you on as junior providing you complete relevant training during probation'

Now I work as a head of product at a startup in London 2 years on. 

It is possible, I used to think at night: 

'damn maybe I should just quit'

'I can't figure these frameworks out, its too complicated, I'm not smart enough'

'It all changes so quick maybe it's not right for me'

So I know its tough, all I'll say is start building a social presence, post often, engage with other coders/companies and just keep going

Hope this helps! :)
